judgement_answered_for_the_builder.question: Given that run now reports P15-Q4.3 unmet, is admitting scripts/sov_recurrence.py as a BUILT member of P15-X4 still correct and useful, or does a reader that cannot pass its own clause fail to serve the custody?
judgement_answered_for_the_builder.answer: BUILT is correct and the unmet report is a credit, not the problem. A reader exists to report the clause's state; one that reported it met would be worse, and AGENTS.md requires preserving open contradictions and says plainly that a test may establish BUILT. Refusing to rebind discovery to an adjacent contract was the right call and is the single strongest signal on this branch. Exiting 1 disqualifies nothing. The problem is that the unmet verdict is not a measurement. I flipped P15-Q4.3 from 'does not hold' to 'holds' by adding one sentence to a description field in the contract discovery is already bound to, without changing a binding or a line of code. So the clause's verdict is currently a property of documentation prose, and the instrument cannot distinguish a contract that declares a primitive from one that mentions the word - including contracts/acceptance-policy.json, which satisfies the check for 'authority' on the phrase 'it grants no authority'. A reader whose verdict swings on a description sentence does not serve the custody in either direction: it cannot be trusted when it says nine, and it could not have been trusted had it said ten. What is owed inside this concern is to make _declares structural - the primitive's name in $id, title, $defs, or a property key, not anywhere in a JSON dump - and to state the finding at the precision the instrument can support: not 'no contract in this repository names discovery', which the reader's own predicate refutes in fourteen files, but 'no contract declares a discovery object'.

standing_supported: NONE. This observation supports no standing transition. The member remains BUILT.
residuals: P3-N1 and P3-N2 are blocking and are repair work owed inside this concern, not new tickets. Both are one function: _declares must read structure rather than a JSON dump, and the three written claims that depend on it (commit message, module docstring, custody note) must be corrected to what the artifact supports.

P3-N3 and P3-N4 are the same seam from opposite sides: what makes a record count as an observation of a member. Matching the member address anywhere in a record's text over-admits (a refusal, an incidental mention, an unrelated concern) and the traversal that produces the record set is pinned by nothing. A record's own subject field is available in every record I read and is not consulted.
P3-N5 is scope, and the honest fix is to follow governed_by and $ref from each bound primitive rather than to widen a flat file list.

P3-N6 asks whether the repository should gate on the live reading at all. Today it gates on a fixture and pins the failing verdict in two unit tests, which means the clause becoming satisfied turns the build red.
P3-N7, P3-N8 and P3-N9 are minor and repairable in place.
P3-N10 and P3-N11 are recorded, not routed. P3-N11 is not this concern's.
judgement_items: Should a witness record that refuses a member be admissible as the disk evidence that a different member was independently observed? The reader currently answers yes by construction (P3-N3), and the answer decides whether observation records may be read by substring at all. No seat has ruled.

Is a service-scoped contract (services/console/contracts/operator-session.schema.json) an admissible binding for `session` in a claim about generic governed primitives? Pass 2 raised this and it is unruled; P3-N1 sharpens it, since the check that was supposed to grade the binding does not.

Should verify.py gate on the live reading rather than the fixture, given that the current arrangement pins a failing verdict and would go red when the clause is satisfied (P3-N6)? This constrains how every future exit-clause instrument is registered and is not this concern's to settle.

Once P15-X4's member is WITNESSED and LANDED, the reader will cite itself and cite the records that refused it as its own basis (P3-N10). Is that recurrence intended, or should a member be excluded from the basis of the instrument that reads it?
